copy.title: The Swift Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Taylor Swift’s family: who owns what, which stocks you can buy, the homes, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #018 · The Swift family · Data as of
copy.h1: The pop star who bought back her masters got married. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them owns, which of their companies you can buy stock in, the homes, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they own, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. Taylor married Travis Kelce in July 2026, so his mother and brother are here too.
copy.investLede: One company here trades on the stock market with family money in it: Six Flags, through an investor group that includes Travis. Taylor’s label, Universal Music Group, is public too, but no stake of hers has been reported.
copy.moneyLede: Forbes says Taylor’s fortune comes from touring, royalties, her music catalog and her homes. Two people on this map have a published net worth.
copy.homesLede: Seven homes in four places, bought from 2009 to 2018. Prices are what she paid, as reported. No street addresses here.
copy.homesFlipLabel: Her real estate, by Forbes’s count
copy.recordLede: The money that shows up in contracts, deal reports and Forbes estimates: the masters, the tour, the label, the podcast. Reported figures, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From West Reading, Pennsylvania, in 1989 to a $2 billion fortune and a wedding at Madison Square Garden.
copy.calcYearsK: Years to earn what Taylor has

summary.t: Former Merrill Lynch stockbroker. The family moved to Tennessee when he transferred to the firm’s Nashville office; Taylor was 14.

record.t: Owned shares in Big Machine Records, Taylor’s first label. It sold to Scooter Braun for a reported $300 million in 2019, and the masters of her first six albums went with it.

summary.t: Worked as a mutual fund marketing executive. Her mother, Marjorie Finlay, was an opera singer whose church singing is one of Taylor’s earliest memories of music.
Mother of Jason and Travis. Spent 30 years in banking, including at Mastercard and in commercial real estate finance.

facts.t: Her sons were the first brothers to play against each other in a Super Bowl.
Appeared in two Hallmark movies in 2024, including Holiday Touchdown: A Chiefs Love Story.

summary.t: Taylor’s younger brother. A music executive, producer and actor; he studied film at Notre Dame and appeared in Live by Night (2016).

facts.t: Executive producer of Folklore: The Long Pond Studio Sessions (2020).
Was Taylor’s man of honor at the July 2026 wedding.

summary.t: Singer-songwriter. Forbes says she is the first musician to become a billionaire mainly from her songs and performances.

owns.t: Bought back the masters of her first six albums on May 30, 2025. Billboard’s sources put the price at around $360 million.

record.t: Grossed $2,077,618,725 from 149 shows and 10,168,008 tickets, March 2023 to December 2024. It was the first tour to pass $2 billion.

Big Machine, the label that owned her first six albums, sold for a reported $300 million in 2019. She bought those masters back from Shamrock in May 2025 for around $360 million, according to Billboard’s sources.
Forbes estimates Disney+ paid about $75 million to stream the Eras Tour film, then about $100 million more for a behind-the-scenes series and a second concert film.
Signed with Universal Music Group’s Republic Records in November 2018. The deal lets her own her master recordings, and UMG agreed to share any Spotify stock sale proceeds with its artists.

facts.t: Forbes first counted her as a billionaire in October 2023. By July 2026, it said her fortune had more than doubled.
Forbes estimates she earned $202 million in 2025, before taxes and fees. It ranked her No. 2 on its 2025 list of the highest-paid musicians.
Married Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden on July 3, 2026. Adam Sandler officiated.

summary.t: Tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs since 2013 and a three-time Super Bowl champion. Co-hosts the New Heights podcast with his brother Jason.

owns.t: Co-hosts it with Jason. In 2024 the brothers signed a three-year deal with Amazon’s Wondery worth more than $100 million; Forbes puts the minimum at $105 million.
Part of Jana Partners’ activist investor group, which disclosed an economic interest of about 9% in October 2025. Six Flags named him a brand ambassador in March 2026; terms weren’t disclosed.

record.t: Signed a two-year, $34.25 million extension in April 2024, a record yearly average for a tight end. In March 2026 he agreed to return for a 14th season on a one-year deal worth up to $15 million, with $12 million guaranteed.
Forbes ranked him No. 8 on its 2025 list of the highest-paid NFL players, with $47.3 million. It estimates $30 million of his 2025 income came off the field, from commercials and the podcast deal.

facts.t: The Chiefs drafted him in the third round in 2013.
His brother Jason was best man at the wedding.

summary.t: Travis’s older brother. Played center for the Philadelphia Eagles for 13 seasons, won Super Bowl LII and retired in March 2024. Joined ESPN as an analyst that year.

owns.t: Co-host since it launched in September 2022. He and Travis signed the Wondery deal in 2024.

facts.t: Launched an ESPN late-night show, They Call It Late Night, in January 2025.
Was Travis’s best man at the July 2026 wedding.
